statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 9% with NQ mid-range of a two-sided overnight band and realised volatility compressed.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays EA_ON. The 13:00-15:00 UTC window spanning the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech is the session's main checkpoint, and the published forecast reaches WATCH there. headline: NQ holds the middle of a 102-point overnight band after its Globex high was retraced, leaving mean reversion intact below Monday's record cash close
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 31,354.50, up 36.75 points (+0.12%) from the 31,317.75 previous close, after the advance to the 31,411.25 Globex high was given back. Price sits 45.25 points above the 31,309.25 overnight low and 56.75 below that high, just under the midpoint of a 102.00-point band worth about 0.33% of index value. That two-sided profile is the decisive observation for the Tail score: the overnight push was retraced rather than extended, and the hour since the previous assessment produced a net four-point drift, which is working mean reversion rather than the persistent no-retracement path this score is built to detect. E-mini S&P 500 futures confirm it, holding a 9.50-point range at 7,833.75, and VIX at 15.52 against a 15.31 prior close shows no bid for protection. The Asian session gave no aligned directional lead either, with the Nikkei up 0.3% and the Hang Seng up 0.8% against a 0.8% fall in Korea. The backdrop is a genuinely strong one: the cash Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 31,076.44, up 0.87%, in a 30,798.42-31,117.36 range, led by semiconductors as Nvidia pushed toward a $6 trillion valuation. That record close is context for what an opening auction may test later, not evidence of current structure, and the published forecast treats it accordingly. The live concern sits in fixed income rather than equities. The 10-year yield rose 3.40 basis points on Monday to 5.3110%, the highest since 2007, the 30-year added 3.45 to 5.6645%, and the French-German spread posted its largest weekly rise since 1990, a bond-equity divergence that market commentary has explicitly flagged while equities sit near records. ISM Services prices paid at 74.0 was the highest since July 2022 even as the employment component softened, and Brent near $100.40 with WTI near $89.54 keeps energy an inflation input, though Hormuz crude flows recovering to 76% of prewar levels points toward de-escalation rather than a new amplifier. None of that has yet transmitted into a one-way index path, so it is carried in Stress at 45% rather than in Tail, which eases to 9%. Confidence is 86%: current futures levels and ranges, the cash close, VIX, Treasury yields, oil, the Asian session and a verified seven-day U.S. calendar were all gathered directly from primary sources, with the shared Finviz context file the one input unavailable because its latest collection is roughly seven days stale and therefore excluded as supporting evidence.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours of published Claude assessments stayed in the low Tail band apart from the 19:00 UTC hour, which reached WATCH at 20% during the U.S. afternoon advance to a record close. Tail ran from 8% in the Asian session on 5 October down to 6% at 08:00 UTC, climbed through the European and U.S. sessions to that 20% peak at 19:00 UTC, then decayed to 9% by 00:00 UTC, printed 12% at 01:00 UTC on a new Globex high and settled between 9% and 10% through 03:00 UTC. Stress fell steadily from 54% to 45% as realised volatility compressed even while long-end yields stayed near multi-decade highs, and Confidence held between 86% and 89% throughout. The 06:00 UTC hour has no published assessment and is recorded as unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of the 24 forecast hours and reaches WATCH only at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC, which span the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech. Tail holds near 9-10% through the thin late-Asian and pre-European hours, steps up from the European cash open at 08:00 UTC, peaks at 20% across the first two U.S. cash hours, then decays through the afternoon with a secondary 17% reading in the power hour before easing to 10% by the Asian session on 7 October. Stress tracks the same shape between 44% and 54%, and Confidence declines from 86% to 78% as distance from the verified overnight price evidence grows. Every hour beyond the current clock hour is conditional: no European or U.S. price path has been observed at assessment time, and the scheduled items in the event calendar are checkpoints rather than assertions about outcomes. The 10-year auction and the FOMC minutes fall on 7 October, after this window closes.
